BestStartCohort.description:
A child's Best Start birth-cohort classification. Not a bool: a child
can be genuinely outside Best Start entitlement altogether (too old --
outside the first-three-years window entirely), or within that general
window but in a birth cohort/period specification.md explicitly puts
outside the v0.1 calculable branch ("later birth cohorts ... require
separate review; do not apply this branch to them") -- collapsing those
two into one `bool` would silently treat "out of this narrow branch,
entitlement genuinely unknown" the same as "verified zero entitlement",
which is exactly the false-zero bug this type exists to prevent.

FactStatus.description:
Tri-state for any fact that gates a component.

One shared tri-state covers both flavours of gate the calculation
contracts use:

- A **domain/eligibility precondition** (e.g. WFF's "in-work eligibility
  established"): `VERIFIED` means the condition holds and the branch may
  proceed; `EXCLUDED` means it's verified *not* to hold, so the scenario
  is structurally outside this branch (`unsupported`); `UNKNOWN` means
  it hasn't been verified either way (`needs_review`).
- A **known exclusion trigger** (e.g. WFF's MD 14/15 protected credit):
  `VERIFIED` means verified that the trigger does *not* apply (the
  ordinary branch proceeds); `EXCLUDED` means verified that it *does*
  apply (`unsupported` -- the protected/direct-abatement/etc. pathway
  needs its own specification); `UNKNOWN` means unverified
  applicability (`needs_review`).

Never a bare `bool`: SCHEMA.md forbids silently defaulting a missing
fact to a value that would yield entitlement, and a bool has no way to
represent "not verified" distinctly from "verified false".
FactStatus.title: FactStatus

PartnerStatus.description:
Whether the claimant has a partner, per specification.md's "one
claimant and a stable partner status" domain precondition -- a
household-level fact, independent of `VerifiedIncome`.

This exists because `VerifiedIncome.partner_amount is None` is
ambiguous on its own: it's the correct shape both for a genuinely single
claimant (no partner to verify) *and* for a partnered claimant whose
partner's income simply wasn't supplied. Those are not the same case --
the second one must be `needs_review`, not silently treated as the
first. `PartnerStatus` is the independent fact that resolves the
ambiguity; see `_partner_income_gap_reason`.
PartnerStatus.title: PartnerStatus

info.description: Deterministic NZ policy calculations. Every input marked 'verified' (household_eligibility, income, etc.) is the caller's own assertion that the underlying fact has been verified elsewhere -- this API does not itself confirm any fact against a government record or other authoritative source. A result is therefore a conditional simulation given the facts the caller asserted, not an independently verified entitlement determination; a `calculated` outcome is only as reliable as the caller's own verification of its inputs.
info.title: Poltika API

post.description:
Calculate Accommodation Supplement entitlement for one scenario.

**This is a conditional simulation, not a verified entitlement
determination.** Every `"verified"` fact in the request is the
caller's own assertion -- Poltika does not independently confirm it
against any government record (see the app-level description in
`poltika.api.main` for the full statement).

Wraps `run_as_module()` directly against the internally-pinned
`policy_specs/accommodation_supplement` directory. A `PoltikaError`
raised by the loader (e.g. a `requested_policy_version` mismatch) is
not caught here -- it propagates to the app-level exception handlers
registered in `poltika.api.main`, which map it to an explicit HTTP
status rather than a 200.

post.description:
Calculate WFF and Accommodation Supplement for one household.

**This is a conditional simulation, not a verified entitlement
determination.** Each policy is reported in its own period, and there is
no combined total. A structural error (such as a policy-version
mismatch) maps to 409 or 500 through the app-level handlers.

When a component is waiting for a fact, `resolution` adds what can be
said without it (ADR-0016): the household rerun for each admissible
answer, with ranges and the most useful next question. Each branch is
an ordinary engine run; nothing conditional is labelled `calculated`.

v0.3 Task 1b.4-1b.5 (ADR-0016): the next question before a run.

- `ask`: the next question for the components asked about, from the
  fact catalogue, with its admissible answers.
- `ready`: nothing blocks them.
- `incomplete`: only declined facts block them; `calculation.resolution`
  gives what can be said without them.

`calculation` is always the household with the answers so far applied.
An answer is the caller's assertion, like every `verified` input. An
inadmissible answer is a 422 naming what is admissible; it is never
coerced. "Don't know" is a declined fact, never a default.

Calculate basic annual income tax for one individual.

**This is a conditional simulation, not a verified determination.**
Every `"verified"` fact and the attested taxable income are the caller's
own assertion; Poltika derives no taxable income. The income-tax policy
is draft, so this route returns `needs_review` or `unsupported` and never
an amount (see this module's docstring).

A `PoltikaError` raised by the loader (e.g. a `requested_policy_version`
mismatch) is not caught here -- it propagates to the app-level handlers
in `poltika.api.main`, which map it to an explicit HTTP status.

post.description:
Run and store a household scenario. **A conditional simulation, not a
verified entitlement determination** (see `/household/calculate`).

Calculate WFF entitlement for one scenario.

**This is a conditional simulation, not a verified entitlement
determination.** Every `"verified"` fact in the request (e.g.
`household_eligibility: "verified"`) is the caller's own assertion --
Poltika does not independently confirm it against any government
record. A `calculated` result is only as reliable as the caller's own
verification of the facts it supplied (see the app-level description
in `poltika.api.main` for the full statement; PR #22 review finding).

Wraps `run_wff_module()` directly against the internally-pinned
`policy_specs/working_for_families` directory. A `PoltikaError` raised
by the loader (e.g. a `requested_policy_version` mismatch) is not
caught here -- it propagates to the app-level exception handlers
registered in `poltika.api.main`, which map it to an explicit HTTP
status rather than a 200.

Each override on its own against the baseline parameters: the value
it would produce, or why it is refused. Nothing is run.
